description: Portable processor scenarios for the OpenAPI 3.2 binding-specification sibling. Configuration is named semantically; adapters normalize HTTP observations.

scenarios.description: The exact 3.2.0 edition is admitted, an operation with omitted responses remains addressable, and a plain empty unary response completes without an output value.
A later patch-looking 3.2 edition is refused at the exact pre-resolution edition gate.
The 3.2 family token does not infer acceptance of a 3.1 artifact.
Selector evaluation never percent-decodes an RFC 6901 path segment.
Root $self establishes the OpenAPI-description base used by a relative selected Path Item reference.
A selected reference that uses a retrieval alias despite the target document's declared $self identity is upstream-invalid at its smallest referencing owner and refuses before dispatch.
A Path Item $ref collision on the selected method excludes that target.
A collision confined to an unused Path Item method does not exclude the selected operation.
Omitting components, paths, and webhooks leaves no possible target position and refuses the whole source after the closed load gates without becoming a fifth load gate.

A root jsonSchemaDialect outside the incorporated base dialect excludes the whole source at source scope, including a schema-free target. The selector reaches no admitted source and therefore refuses at resolution; this is not a defect-derived source refusal.
A present empty Responses Object is upstream-invalid and removes the selected target as invalid, while omission remains addressable.

Reference identity applies through the selected request closure: a Request Body reference using a retrieval alias instead of the target document's $self identity is upstream-invalid at its smallest referencing owner.
A selected Schema Object reference cannot cross a nearer $id resource boundary using the containing OpenAPI document plus a deep pointer.
A selected Response Object reference using a retrieval alias instead of the target document's declared $self identity is upstream-invalid and unresolvable, so invocation refuses before dispatch.
An unsupported $schema at a selected schema-resource root excludes the selected operation while the source itself remains admitted.
A duplicate YAML mapping key refuses at the accepted-representation grammar gate.
A multi-document YAML stream refuses because exactly one document is admitted.
A YAML value with no JSON data-model image refuses at the compatibility gate.
A non-object root refuses at the closed root-shape load gate.
An object root without the required string openapi field refuses at edition discrimination.
An unusable root $self does not fall back semantically to the retrieval URI for a selected relative reference.
An unresolvable reference confined to an unused sibling operation does not destroy the selected target.
A resolvable cyclic Schema Object graph terminates reference traversal and remains usable.
The fixed query field dispatches the uppercase QUERY method, and QUERY carries its declared request content as the query operation rather than deleting it as GET-like content.
An additionalOperations key retains its exact authored capitalization in both selector identity and the HTTP method sent on the wire.
Additional-operation lookup is byte-exact, so a case-changed selector names no operation and never dispatches.
An additionalOperations map key containing a slash is not an HTTP token even when the selector escapes that map-key segment exactly.
An additionalOperations key byte-equal to the token the fixed query field sends is upstream-invalid and is removed as its own invalid entry.
A colliding upstream-invalid additional-operation entry does not remove the distinct fixed QUERY operation on the same Path Item.
RFC 6901 escaping applies once to an additional method key, so F~0O selects and dispatches the exact F~O HTTP token.
Selector evaluation resolves a referenced Path Item before reading an additionalOperations entry and composes a non-colliding adjacent entry.
The same additional-operation key in a referenced and adjacent Path Item is an undefined selected-field collision and excludes that target.
A Path Item $ref collision confined to an unused additional-operation key does not exclude a different selected additional operation.
A TRACE requestBody declaration creates no required caller body and a body-free invocation dispatches TRACE without content.
A supplied caller body on TRACE is unroutable and refuses before dispatch even when the artifact declares requestBody.
The caller correspondence is closed to parameters and body, so an unknown top-level key refuses before dispatch.
A present caller-envelope parameters member must be an object and refuses before dispatch otherwise.
Cross-location same-name parameters activate qualified mode for every parameter and remain independently writable through location/RFC6901-name keys.
Once cross-location duplication activates qualified mode, the bare parameter name is unknown and refuses before dispatch.
A present body member carrying JSON null is supplied rather than absent and crosses the correspondence boundary as the one JSON null body value.
Omission of a required request body remains distinct from supplied null and refuses before dispatch.
An unknown key inside the parameters object refuses before dispatch; no unmatched-field passthrough exists even without a body.
A form-urlencoded querystring Parameter supplies the complete raw query component; its authored parameter name is not serialized and the result receives no second escaping pass.
A non-urlencoded JSON querystring representation is percent-encoded as one complete query component with uppercase percent triplets.
An operation-level querystring Parameter colliding with an ordinary query Parameter inherited from its Path Item is upstream-invalid and removes the target before input inspection.
More than one effective querystring Parameter across Path Item and Operation owners is upstream-invalid and removes the selected target as invalid.
A querystring Parameter with an explicitly present schema-form field is excluded even when that field equals its typed default.
A whole null in the matrix path cell serializes as the name-only matrix segment ;id.
A whole null in the label path cell serializes as the label prefix alone.
A whole null in the simple path cell serializes as the empty string.
Whole null values in the form query and cookie cells serialize as present empty name=value contributions.
A whole null in the spaceDelimited query cell is n/a and refuses before dispatch.
A null member inside an array has no RFC 6570 representation and refuses before dispatch.
deepObject ignores an explicit explode false value and emits its brackets percent-encoded exactly as the 3.2 style example.
Manual allowReserved query construction still percent-encodes square brackets, fragment, query-pair, equals, and plus delimiters while retaining other permitted reserved bytes.
The pipeDelimited query separator is emitted as uppercase %7C rather than a raw non-RFC-6570 delimiter.
The 3.2 cookie style admits repeated array pairs and gives whole null its defined empty value, joined by the RFC 6265 semicolon-space separator.
Omission of a required non-path Parameter refuses before dispatch on the 3.2 lane.
A style-location cell outside the closed 3.2 table excludes the selected target before caller values are inspected.
A resolved object member that is itself compound has no defined style expansion and statically excludes the target.
An effective path Parameter without a matching template expression is upstream-invalid and removes the target under exact one-to-one correspondence.
A path-template expression appearing more than once violates OAS 3.2's exact one-to-one correspondence and removes the target as invalid.
Two templated path keys with an equivalent static hierarchy are upstream-invalid and remove either selected target as invalid.
A JSON content-form query Parameter serializes first and then percent-encodes that entire representation as one value.
A querystring media entry with itemSchema selects a sequential representation and excludes the target because a stream has no query-component mapping.
Supplying both a raw Cookie Header Parameter and a structured cookie Parameter refuses before dispatch rather than merging them.
An optional 3.2 exploded form-cookie array remains represented, and omitting it dispatches without a Cookie field.
A supplied JSON number on a schema-form Parameter refuses when parameterConversion is not configured; no canonical spelling is inferred.
allowEmptyValue true preserves a supplied empty query string as a present empty name=value pair.
A querystring Parameter sharing its name with a Header Parameter activates qualified mode and each location remains independently writable.

Exactly one usable concrete request media entry self-selects and strict JSON rides as UTF-8; the only declared response body belongs to 204 and is excluded by the no-content rule, so no response-media range survives from which to generate Accept.
Two usable concrete request alternatives require requestMedia before input consumption; the supplied value never elects one.
A concrete requestMedia value matching two declarations at equal exact-and-parameter specificity refuses instead of using map order.
An absent optional body bypasses a multi-alternative request media map and emits neither body nor Content-Type.
text/json is character data rather than JSON and carries a sole-string declaration without adding JSON quotes.
A boolean non-JSON text value serializes as exactly true under its declaration-selected character lane.
A non-JSON text number uses the shortest exact spelling, preferring 1e3 over the longer non-exponent 1000.
A supplied null on the nullable-string character lane refuses because that lane defines no null lexical form.
A schema-omitted concrete non-JSON body uses canonical Base64 at the OpenBindings boundary and dispatches the decoded octets.
A non-canonical raw-octet boundary string with missing Base64 padding refuses before dispatch.
A sole-string declaration with contentEncoding carries the artifact-encoded characters unchanged rather than Base64-decoding them.
An object-valued XML alternative is excluded because the incorporated authority does not determine all XML bytes.
Explicit allowReserved false is still field presence: it selects the form style path, ignores contentType, and spells a space as percent-20 rather than plus.
A name-based Encoding key with no corresponding property is ignored and does not disturb the declared property.
A name-based multipart array emits one part per item in order under the repeated property name.

A string part with contentEncoding remains artifact text and emits NO Content-Transfer-Encoding header: OAS 3.2.0's equivalence sentence describes what the declaration means, and the section's own note plus RFC 7578 section 4.7 (senders SHOULD NOT generate the field) settle non-emission (ruling R5, 2026-09-01).
An explicit part transfer Header that disallows the schema contentEncoding excludes that field and refuses an invocation that reaches it.
Positional multipart emits one part per array item in order, applying prefixEncoding by position and itemEncoding to the remainder.
Name-based encoding combined with positional itemEncoding invalidates only that multipart alternative; a JSON sibling remains selectable.
Positional multipart/form-data refuses when the applicable Encoding Object has no fixed Content-Disposition name.
A Content-Disposition Header default does not fix a positional form-data part name; only const or a single-member enum does.
One active nested Encoding level recursively serializes an array property as a multipart/mixed part containing its ordered items.
An alternative requiring more than one nested Encoding level is unavailable and refuses when it is the only request representation.
A JSON Lines request consumes one caller array and emits one JSON item per line while allowing schema and itemSchema to coexist.
A +json-seq request frames each JSON item with record separator and line feed in array order.
text/event-stream is excluded on requests because incorporated authority supplies no object-to-event write algorithm.
itemSchema on a media type with no incorporated sequential framing excludes only that request alternative rather than treating it as ordinary JSON.
A components.mediaTypes reference resolves before positional multipart lane selection, and its raw Encoding overlay remains attached to the selected artifact.
A typeless form-urlencoded property takes its application/octet-stream default, decodes the canonical Base64 boundary, and percent-encodes the resulting octets.
A typeless name-based multipart property uses the raw-octet lane and its application/octet-stream part default.
A wildcard Encoding contentType requires one concrete propertyMedia choice for the affected property before input consumption.
A concrete propertyMedia choice matching a wildcard Encoding member fixes the part Content-Type without changing that property's raw-octet boundary.
A supplied null optional property on the content-based form path is elided while unaffected sibling fields remain.
A required nullable content-based form property cannot be silently elided; a supplied null therefore refuses before dispatch.
Encoding, prefixEncoding, and itemEncoding are ignored on application/json even when their nested contents would be unavailable on multipart.
Nested Encoding fields are ignored when their governing part Content-Type is explicitly non-multipart.

A concrete requestMedia choice materializes the declared text media range but cannot turn a merely supplied boolean into OAS validated runtime data. The multi-type schema does not determine one non-JSON serialization type, so invocation refuses before dispatch without inspecting the supplied value's apparent type.
A concrete requestMedia choice materializes JSON Lines framing and itemSchema through a declared media range.
An absent optional body bypasses request media planning even when its only authored alternative has no request write algorithm.
Empty operation and Path Item server arrays supply no local alternative, so resolution falls through to the root Server Object.
Several effective Server Objects require the typed server configuration point; authored order supplies no preference.
A selected Server Object receives exact supplied variable values, and those values satisfy the declaration's nonempty enum.
A repeated Server Variable is upstream-invalid and removes only its Server alternative as invalid; the sole surviving sibling self-selects.
A supplied Server Variable value outside its declared enum refuses before dispatch.
Embedded content with no location cannot resolve a relative Server URL even when root $self is absolute, because $self is not the API URL base.
With a co-present retrieval location, a relative root Server URL resolves against retrieval rather than the different absolute $self identity.
A query-bearing Server URL is upstream-invalid and removes only that alternative as invalid; its valid sibling remains the sole usable server.
Path append removes exactly the redundant seam slash: a trailing Server slash and leading operation slash produce one slash, not two.

A complete consumer-configured URL replaces the resolved server base, and the operation's path bytes join to it under the preceding boundary rule; the artifact's path template, path substitution, query construction, method, parameters, body, response, and security semantics remain unchanged.
Two complete security alternatives require explicit security selection even when runtime credentials satisfy both.
An operation-level empty security array overrides root security and never volunteers unrelated credentials.
An apiKey query credential uses the exact destination and Section 8.2 percent encoding.
An apiKey cookie containing a semicolon cannot be carried as an RFC 6265 cookie-value and refuses without percent-encoding recovery.
A credential collision excludes only its complete alternative; explicitly selecting a non-colliding sibling emits only that sibling's credential.
A malformed Security Scheme Object is upstream-invalid and removes only alternatives requiring it as invalid; a selected valid sibling remains dispatchable.
A Security Requirement URI identifies its Security Scheme Object and retains the exact URI spelling as the runtime credential identity.
A ./-disambiguated relative Security Requirement URI is loaded as an artifact resource and bypasses component-name scope selection.
The serialized actual request Content-Encoding field fixes the runtime encoder stack; the encoder transforms the complete representation and the field remains on the wire.
The native 3.2 response lane round-trips one non-sequential exact-status JSON response as one unary operation value.
Reference closure follows a Reference Object reached through a Security Requirement URI while preserving the authored requirement spelling as credential identity.
Cookie style defaults omitted explode to true, so an array emits repeated RFC 6265 pairs joined by the semicolon-space separator.
An exact final-status response overrides its matching class range and default; the 3.2 Response Object needs no description field to govern.
The single matching response-key range governs ahead of default while native final-status classification remains successful for an unlisted 2xx code.
A lowercase response range is outside the closed exact/range/default/extension key set and removes the selected target as invalid before dispatch.
An exact response key outside the five admitted HTTP status classes removes the selected target as invalid before any actual response is inspected.
A governing non-Content-Type Header Object declaring required true makes the actual header mandatory even when the successful response body is empty.
A response Header Object named Content-Type is ignored even when it declares required true, so its absence cannot fail an empty response.
A normalized response-media collision is confined to that identity; a clean sibling declaration still governs decoding.
An actual response selecting a normalized-colliding media identity is a loud protocol error; map order cannot choose a winner.
A non-empty response without Content-Type assumes application/octet-stream before matching and emits the exact octets through the canonical Base64 value boundary.
A zero-octet successful response emits no output value even when its governing declaration names JSON; it never manufactures null or an empty string.
A non-empty actual response with no governing exact, range, or default Response Object is a loud protocol error.
A response to HEAD is empty by definition even if a scripted peer supplies payload octets; no operation output value is emitted.
A default-governed non-2xx final response remains unsuccessful while its JSON body is preserved as opaque application-authored failure data rather than an operation output.

The actual response Content-Encoding value fixes the decoder stack, which runs in reverse wire order before the selected media lane; its governing Header Object constrains the field but does not authorize decoding.

A response content-coding token admitted by the governing Header Object is unsupported by runtime capability. The condition is never skipped or sniffed, and the response-side condition is a loud protocol error.

Content-coding implementations are runtime capabilities, not binding configuration points. The actual Content-Encoding field fixes the coding stack even though the governing Response Object omits a Header Object for that field; an absent declaration therefore imposes no content-coding constraint and does not declare identity.
A runtime response decoder supplies capability but cannot make an actual coding value satisfy a conflicting governing Header Object constraint.
The actual identity response coding is admitted by the governing Header Object, requires no runtime decoder, and preserves the representation for the selected media lane.
The runtime responseContentCodings capability map matches actual content-coding tokens case-insensitively.
Case-insensitive response Content-Encoding declarations form one conjunctive group; an unconstrained pair accepts the one actual identity field and the response completes.
An application/jsonl success response emits one parsed JSON operation value per line in wire order.
The application/x-ndjson spelling uses the same ordered newline-delimited JSON item boundary.
An application/json-seq response uses RS framing and emits each parsed JSON text in order.
A +json-seq structured-suffix response uses the incorporated JSON text sequence framing without media sniffing.
A positional multipart success response emits one decoded part value per item in part order.
A malformed later JSON Lines item is not emitted and ends the interaction unsuccessfully while an earlier valid item remains a successful value.
itemSchema on a media type with no incorporated item framing makes that selected response alternative unavailable rather than authorizing sniffing.
A non-successful final status keeps a sequential response body in failure data and emits no successful item values.
A non-sequential application/json response remains unary even when its complete-response schema is an array.
The consumer delivery bound applies independently to each sequential item; an oversized later item fails after an earlier bounded item was emitted.
A selected external Response Object addressed through its declared $self identity composes its response content into the target.
A 3.2 Media Type Object Reference addressed through the external document's canonical $self identity is loaded as part of the selected response closure.
A Media Type Object reference using a retrieval alias makes only that response media invalid; a sibling media alternative remains usable.
An actual response selecting the unavailable retrieval-alias Media Type alternative fails loudly without falling back to its sibling.
A response Schema Object reference crossing a nearer $id boundary noncanonically is upstream-invalid only at its media-alternative owner, leaving a sibling response media usable.
An actual response selecting a media alternative whose Schema reference crosses a nearer $id boundary fails loudly without choosing a sibling declaration.
Fields added beside a Response Reference Object are ignored and do not extend the selected response closure.
A cyclic but resolvable selected Response Reference graph terminates and remains legitimate.
An unresolvable response reference outside the selected target-plus-reachable closure does not affect the selected operation.
A canonical external Header Object reference is part of the selected response closure and governs the actual required response header.
A response Header Object reference using a retrieval alias instead of its document's declared $self identity is invalid and makes the selected response closure unresolvable before dispatch.

A response Link Object reference is part of the response closure even though Link carriage is outside the operation value; using a retrieval alias is upstream-invalid and makes the target unresolvable.

OAS 3.2.0 §§4.14.3.1, 4.14.4, and 4.14.6.3 require ordered per-item processing for sequential media and model each parsed text/event-stream item as the applicable data/event/id/retry object. This seed uses the edition's worked SSE bytes and equivalent JSON records [CO32-12, CO32-13].

peer.body:
event: addString
data: This data is formatted
data: across two lines
retry: 5

event: addInt64
data: 1234.5678
unknownField: this is ignored

: This is a comment
event: addJSON
data: {"foo": 42}

equals.data:
This data is formatted
across two lines

scenarios.description: A supplied value whose shape exits the admitted style-table cell refuses before dispatch at that Parameter: a nested object under a typeless deepObject declaration never serializes through a private spelling.
A JSON Lines final item ended by the end of the stream without a trailing LF is a complete item, and a trailing LF terminates the final item without creating a further item.
An empty line inside a JSON Lines response is a malformed item that ends the interaction unsuccessfully; the earlier valid item remains a successful value.
A present non-string response description is documentary coverage loss only on OAS 3.2; the valid sibling content declaration still governs and decodes the successful JSON response.
A response defect confined to one target does not affect a sibling operation in the same source; selecting the intact sibling still resolves, dispatches, and completes.
A non-map response headers member is confined to that invalid projection and imposes no constraint; the valid sibling content declaration still governs and decodes the successful JSON response.
A non-map response content member is confined to that invalid projection and does not remove the target; an empty successful response dispatches and completes with no output.
A non-map response links member is confined to unused coverage; the valid sibling content declaration still governs and decodes the successful JSON response.
A non-Header response member is confined to that projection while a valid required header sibling still governs; one actual X-Good field satisfies it and the JSON body decodes.
A response defect confined to one target does not affect a sibling operation in the same source; selecting the intact sibling still resolves, dispatches, and completes.

A defect in a Response Object that can never govern a 2xx — here an exact 404 — does not remove the target, because failure data is best-effort. The target whose success path is intact still resolves and dispatches; synthesis separately accounts the invalid 404 Response projection as coverage loss.

`default` is a governing success declaration only when no `2XX` range key covers the success class. Where a `2XX` key is declared, `default` can never govern a 2xx, so a fixed-field defect in it destroys no representation and the target still resolves and dispatches.

An empty successful response has zero content octets and emits no operation output value, so it completes even when the peer stamps a `Content-Type` matching no governing content declaration: an empty body contradicts no media declaration. The governing Response Object declares no content at all here.
A content-map key spelled with an uppercase type and subtype selects the same JSON lane and emits the elected media type normalized to lowercase on the request Content-Type.
A charset parameter value compares ASCII case-insensitively, so a requestMedia choice differing from the declared key only in charset case matches that declaration and elects its lane.

Every media-type parameter value other than charset compares by exact character sequence, so a requestMedia choice differing from the declared key only in boundary case matches no declaration and refuses before dispatch.
A multipart election carries a boundary parameter on the emitted request Content-Type alongside the elected concrete media type.
Every emitted name-based part carries a Content-Disposition field whose disposition type is form-data and whose name parameter holds the property name as a quoted-string.
A property name containing CR and LF cannot be represented as the multipart name parameter and excludes that multipart alternative, leaving the body-emitting invocation with no admissible candidate.

A boundary delimiter line followed by linear whitespace still delimits on the receive side: the comparison takes the boundary at the beginning of the line and does not require an exact match of the entire candidate line.
Anything before the first boundary delimiter line or after the last one is ignored on the receive side, so a preamble and an epilogue contribute no operation value.

peer.body:
preamble a non-MIME reader would show
--b
Content-Type: application/json

{"n":1}
--b--
epilogue text

scenarios.description: A Schema Object default documents the receiver's assumption and is never inserted: an unsupplied optional parameter carrying a default is omitted before serialization exactly as one carrying none, while a supplied sibling still contributes its pair.
A supplied raw-octet value that is not a JSON string refuses before dispatch: the lane's canonical Base64 boundary admits no other JSON type and no repair is applied.

A successful response whose single Content-Type field value is a list of media types selects no media type and is a loud protocol error; no member is picked and the octet-stream assumption does not reach a present field.
On an unsuccessful response the same list-valued Content-Type matches no governing content declaration, so the best-effort failure-body rule yields no failure-data value and raises no protocol error.

A sequential operation value already emitted stands when a later loud protocol error arises in the lane chain rather than in the framing: a later well-framed JSON Lines item carrying a lone surrogate escape yields no value and ends the interaction unsuccessfully.

An API-key credential targeting the processor-owned Accept destination makes the selected security alternative unusable and refuses before dispatch, because a credential there would decide a response-media negotiation question this binding has closed.
That Accept collision compares ASCII case-insensitively like every other API-key header destination, so a lowercase accept destination is the same collision.

On a content-carrying source an elective retrieval from the co-present location is never observable: the retrieved artifact does not replace content, and the completed target comes from the interpreted artifact the document itself carries.

An unquoted numeric Responses key loads and the operation completes. YAML's Core schema resolves the plain scalar 200 to tag:yaml.org,2002:int, but an OpenAPI document is itself a JSON object that YAML merely represents, so the key is the JSON member name it spells. This is the ordinary OpenAPI YAML idiom.

source.content:
openapi: 3.2.0
info:
  title: T
  version: '1'
servers:
  - url: https://api.example
paths:
  /x:
    get:
      responses:
        204:
          description: ok

scenarios.description: A plain scalar key never refuses on its resolved type, whichever Core-schema tag that resolution assigns: an unquoted true in key position is the member name it spells, and the document loads.

scenarios.description: A lowercase additionalOperations key spells a method token no fixed Operation field sends, so it is admitted and dispatched in its authored capitalization beside the fixed post field.
The fixed post field on that same Path Item remains a distinct target and still sends the uppercase POST token.

info.title: fixed field beside its case-distinct sibling

scenarios.description: An additionalOperations key byte-equal to POST is an upstream-invalid entry for the method the post fixed field defines, so it is removed as invalid and never dispatches.

The invoke half of the unsatisfiable-property accounting: the part `bad` admits no instance, so it is not a routed field, and a value supplied for it fails every admission test and refuses before dispatch at that part (Section 5.2). No request is emitted. A processor that dropped the value silently and dispatched the remaining parts would be sending a request the caller did not describe; one that excluded the target at synthesis would have removed an operation on a defect nothing reaches (the companion synthesis scenario pins that half).

expected.description: No request is emitted: the supplied `bad` value reaches a part no value can satisfy.

scenarios.description: A supplied empty string for a query Parameter that declares no allowEmptyValue serializes as the form row's empty cell, q=: the edition's Style Examples define the empty string's bytes independently of allowEmptyValue, and the empty string is not undefined.

A body-free invocation of a `trace` target whose Operation declares an optional `requestBody` dispatches with method TRACE, no body, and no Content-Type field, the optional-declaration companion of OAPI32-PS-35. Section 7: TRACE alone is forbidden content: a client MUST NOT send content, so this binding emits no TRACE body under any declaration (RFC 9110 Section 9.3.8), and Content-Type indicates the media type of the associated representation (RFC 9110 Section 8.3), so a request carrying no representation carries no such field. The same wire fact is pinned on every 3.x sibling. Whether a runtime's platform HTTP API can send TRACE at all is a host limit outside this specification: a runtime that cannot refuses before dispatch, and never dispatches another method in its place.

A required request body with two usable concrete media alternatives and no requestMedia choice is context-required before dispatch. The portable scenario asserts only the binding-specification outcome; target, durability, and challenge-record layout belong to an invocation interface's own conformance suite.

A 3.2 content-based form property whose explicit single concrete Encoding contentType is application/json carries a supplied integer and boolean as their JSON images with a configured parameterConversion never consulted: Section 8.1 names the converter for schema-form parameter serialization and Section 9.3 Encoding/style serialization of form or multipart property values, and an explicit single concrete value fixes the part type under Section 9.3.

Appended is pinned here to one and only one seam repair: the implied root server and the Paths key are joined by removing only their redundant seam slash. A Paths key beginning // therefore retains its intentional doubled slash, distinguishing the narrow join from both verbatim concatenation and broad slash normalization.

A text lane whose type decision encounters $dynamicRef is excluded at that media alternative because the binding does not perform JSON Schema dynamic-scope evaluation; a supplied string cannot turn the reference into a static walk.

An exact uppercase CONNECT additional operation remains addressable but is excluded because successful CONNECT creates a tunnel outside the unary operation model; its selector resolves and invocation refuses before dispatch.
An API-key security alternative whose declared header destination is not an HTTP token is excluded before any credential value is inspected.
A 204 response cannot carry content. Even when the governing Response Object declares text content, actual response bytes are a loud protocol error and are never decoded into an output value.
A non-token optional ordinary Header Parameter is excluded only at that projection; omitting it leaves the operation dispatchable.
The would-be caller key of an excluded optional non-token Header Parameter is unknown input and refuses before dispatch.
A non-token required ordinary Header Parameter excludes its addressable target, whose invocation refuses before dispatch.
An ordinary Header Parameter cannot give the caller control of Transfer-Encoding; the addressable target is excluded and refuses before dispatch.
A 101 response is an immediate loud response-phase protocol error because this unary binding has no upgraded-protocol continuation; the processor does not wait for another HTTP response.

A non-HTTP artifact Server does not destroy the addressable or represented operation, but the artifact-derived completed target refuses before dispatch. The same represented target can proceed with a conforming complete URL, so this missing context is the context-required refusal species.
A complete configured HTTPS URL replaces a non-HTTP artifact Server and dispatches the otherwise unchanged operation.
A non-token optional cookie Parameter is excluded only at that projection; omitting it leaves the operation dispatchable.
The would-be caller key of an excluded optional non-token cookie Parameter is unknown input and refuses before dispatch.
A non-token required cookie Parameter excludes its addressable target, whose invocation refuses before dispatch.
A non-token required response Header Object key excludes its response alternative; a successful response governed by it is a loud response-phase protocol error.
A content-form cookie Parameter whose exact serialized value is not an RFC 6265 cookie-value refuses before dispatch; the binding neither escapes nor repairs it.
A default-only Responses Object is valid, and its fallback Response Object governs an otherwise unmatched successful status.
A leading SP is field-line whitespace rather than part of an RFC 9110 field-value, so an ordinary Header Parameter cannot preserve it and refuses before dispatch.
A raw Cookie Header Parameter must serialize to a complete RFC 6265 cookie-string; a value without a cookie-pair refuses before dispatch.
A header apiKey credential ending in HTAB is not an RFC 9110 field-value and refuses before dispatch.
A selected header apiKey named Cookie is a raw Cookie source; combining it with a supplied structured cookie Parameter refuses before dispatch.
A selected header apiKey named Cookie and a selected cookie apiKey in the same AND requirement are raw and structured Cookie sources; combining them refuses before dispatch.
Case-equivalent required Encoding headers with conflicting exact artifact values exclude the multipart alternative rather than selecting a key by case or map order.
An omitted optional parameter creates no collision; the selected credential emits once and dispatches.
A supplied optional parameter and selected credential that reach the same actual field refuse before dispatch.
An exploded runtime object remains admitted statically, then refuses when its actual serialized token destination collides with a selected query credential.
A required ordinary Proxy-Authorization parameter is excluded at the target boundary because that field authenticates to the first inbound proxy, not the origin API.
Ordinary and credential query contributions form one unordered multiset while preserving each contribution's encoded bytes.
A required whole-querystring parameter excludes only the query-credential alternative; an anonymous OR alternative remains selectable.
An omitted optional whole-querystring parameter leaves the query-credential alternative usable.
Supplying both an optional whole-querystring representation and a selected query credential refuses that invocation rather than overwriting or concatenating either source.
A supplied zero-byte whole-querystring representation emits a present empty query component, unlike omission of the optional parameter.
An anonymous TRACE alternative survives and dispatches without volunteered credential fields.
A TRACE target whose sole alternative emits a credential refuses before dispatch.
A generated multipart name uses UTF-8, emits qdtext literally, and escapes only DQUOTE and backslash with one quoted-pair.
A followed cross-origin redirect strips binding-selected header credentials and does not append the original query credential to the Location target.
An admitted extension method preserves its declared required request body and dispatches the JSON representation instead of treating an unregistered method as content-forbidding.
Supplying request Content-Encoding on an invocation that emits no request representation refuses before dispatch.
Every emitted style-cookie pair name is validated after object expansion; a runtime key containing a semicolon refuses before dispatch.
A case-insensitive HTTP bearer scheme consumes one valid b64token and constructs the exact Authorization field.
A valid OAuth2 Bearer token uses the same exact RFC 6750 Authorization construction.
A valid OpenID Connect Bearer token uses the same exact RFC 6750 Authorization construction.
An empty HTTP bearer credential cannot satisfy b64token and refuses before dispatch.
A space inside an OAuth2 access token is outside b64token and refuses before dispatch.
CR/LF in an OpenID Connect token is outside b64token and refuses before dispatch without emitting a field.
An explicitly non-Bearer OAuth2 runtime token has no carriage under this identifier and refuses before dispatch.

HEAD carries a syntactically valid, declaration-admitted Content-Encoding field but no content octets. The installed Brotli decoder fails if called, so successful empty completion proves the method-based no-content rule does not invoke it.

A 304 response carries a syntactically valid, declaration-admitted Content-Encoding field but no content octets. A failing Brotli sentinel is installed, but the no-content rule does not invoke it. Because 304 is not successful, completion remains the native unsuccessful response.

A non-UTF-8 character request lane requires its direction-specific encoder. With no such runtime capability, encoding refuses before dispatch rather than being reported as a response error or silently substituted.

On a successful HEAD response, resolving the Header schema $ref and filtering the mixed enum yields the exact domain containing only identity. The wire value 7 therefore fails; ignoring the reference or stringifying the numeric enum member would incorrectly complete.

A Server Variable Object missing its REQUIRED default is upstream-invalid at the Server alternative. With no surviving declaration-derived alternative or configured recovery, invocation refuses before dispatch. The same represented target can proceed with a conforming complete URL, so this missing context is the context-required refusal species.

A successful HEAD response still validates Content-Encoding field grammar before the no-content rule suppresses decoding; a non-token coding-list member fails loudly even though no decoder is invoked.
A successful HEAD response still applies its governing exact raw-string Content-Encoding domain; gzip is outside the declared br domain and fails loudly without invoking a content decoder.

Request and response character codecs are independent directional capabilities. The request encoder is installed and permits dispatch, while the response decoder is a failing sentinel and therefore produces a loud response-phase error.

A successful HEAD response evaluates nested allOf constraints recursively. The outer domain admits identity or br, but the nested exact domain admits only identity, so br fails; a shallow implementation would incorrectly complete.
A URL expression without a matching Server Variable declaration is not excluded, but an invocation that supplies no exact substitution is context-required on configuration.server.
An exact consumer substitution completes a URL expression even when the Server Object has no matching Server Variable declaration.

A 204 response carries a syntactically valid, declaration-admitted Content-Encoding field but no content octets. The installed Brotli decoder fails if called, so successful empty completion proves the status-based no-content rule does not invoke it.

Case-equivalent response Header declarations govern conjunctively rather than by first-key selection. The first identity domain admits the actual field, but the second br domain rejects it, so the response fails loudly.

Case-equivalent response Header declarations govern conjunctively rather than by last-key selection. The first br domain rejects the actual field, although the second identity domain admits it, so the response fails loudly.

A caller-supplied JSON request value containing one unpaired surrogate code unit refuses before dispatch. The corpus materializes U+D800 after parsing its JSON-safe template so neither U+FFFD replacement nor an emitted lone-surrogate escape can masquerade as the supplied value.

A lone-surrogate escape in a unary JSON response yields no value and is a loud response-phase protocol error; neither U+FFFD replacement nor invalid-Unicode passthrough preserves the received text. This isolates the JSON boundary from the sequential commit behavior exercised separately.

An excluded optional non-token header projection sharing its declared name with a surviving query parameter is removed before caller-key uniqueness is computed; the surviving query parameter therefore uses its unqualified key and dispatches.
Because the removed header projection does not activate qualified mode, the would-be qualified query key is unknown input and refuses before dispatch.

Every admitted response-content media alternative is advertised once at equal preference in deterministic normalized order, while a case-insensitive q parameter is confined to its excluded alternative and cannot become an Accept weight.
A generated multipart Content-Disposition carries the declared part name and invents neither filename nor filename*.
An admissible artifact-fixed Content-Disposition may carry a literal filename and is emitted verbatim rather than replaced or derived from the supplied value.
An artifact-fixed multipart/form-data Content-Disposition containing filename* excludes that media alternative under RFC 7578 and refuses before dispatch when it is the only required request lane.

An admissible artifact-fixed Content-Disposition on another name-based multipart subtype may carry filename* and is emitted verbatim; RFC 7578's filename* prohibition is specific to multipart/form-data.
A present caller-envelope value that is not a JSON object is outside the closed envelope grammar and refuses before dispatch; it is never treated as a body value or parameter map.
An optional exploded form-cookie array remains represented, and a supplied one-item value emits exactly one Cookie pair.
A required exploded form-cookie object remains represented, and a supplied one-property value emits exactly one Cookie pair under that property's name.
OAS 3.2 non-exploded form-cookie arrays remain admitted and percent-encode reserved data inside a single member rather than entering the exploded wrong-delimiter path.
A typeless exploded form-cookie declaration survives static analysis, but a supplied array would emit multiple pairs with the wrong delimiter and refuses.
A required Request Body whose sole object-model XML alternative is excluded has no surviving effective request-content alternative and excludes the target.
Accept advertises admitted media from both success and failure Responses, but a failure-only problem media type cannot govern an actual 200 response.
A fixed-operation PATCH preserves its required JSON Request Body and emits PATCH under RFC 5789 rather than treating the method as body-undefined.
A fixed-operation PATCH with a required Request Body refuses before dispatch when the caller omits the body.
A supplied empty array is present rather than omitted and uses the form undefined-value cell, emitting one empty Cookie pair rather than disappearing or entering the multi-pair refusal path.
An admitted additionalOperations extension method with a required Request Body refuses before dispatch when the caller omits that body; extension status does not weaken required-body enforcement.
